take_homes: Access and absorption are different numbers. Licences or 'they can reach it' tell me nothing about whether anyone uses it.
Before building something for non-engineers, find the one person and the job they do today. My candidate has to beat their spreadsheet or their colleague, not just exist.
Write the people plan as seriously as the technical one. Mine had unnamed roles, and that was the finding.

monday.move: Ask the head of sales, or one rep, how they prepare for a customer call today, and what would make them drop that for something I built. No building until I have the answer.
monday.who: One sales rep I trust, plus the sales lead
monday.stop_condition: If they can't name a recurring job where an agent would save real time, or nobody will own it after the first month, I stop the org-wide idea.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering asked for this, and I haven't worked out who maintains it. I'll also want to start building the weekend version before the call.

misconception.why: My technical plan looked fine and my people plan was empty. That is one case of good output with the checking missing. I still skipped the spot-checks on the jtbd and bottleneck files and don't think they're needed. The 'checking is for beginners' belief weakened about the plans, not about the agent's output.

one_line: Skip the grey filler boxes. The scar story and the 'what would have to be true to switch' question are worth the hour. It slowed me down once, when my people plan turned out empty.
